question.text: An 87-year-old female patient presents with episodic mood swings and coordination difficulties over the past six months. She has a notable history of hypertension and diabetes. Her primary care provider suspects Emotional Intensity Disease (EID) linked to the Glianorex based on the clinical presentation. Which of the following best represents the series of diagnostic assessments to confirm EID and rule out other conditions?

options.A: Begin with a complete psychological evaluation using standardized questionnaires, followed by neuroimaging studies including fMRI to assess brain activity, and finally GIS to visualize the Glianorex.
options.B: Start with serum analysis of Equilibron and Neurostabilin levels to identify hormonal imbalances, proceed to GIS to examine the structure of the Glianorex, and conclude with a psychometric evaluation.
options.C: Conduct an initial comprehensive patient history and physical exam to identify mood and coordination irregularities, followed by biochemical marker analysis including cortisol and neurotransmitter metabolites, then use GIS and neuroimaging techniques for further insights.
options.D: Execute a psychological assessment to determine emotional dysregulation, use PET scans to map neural patterns involved in emotional processing, and end with GIS combined with neurochemical analysis.
options.F: I don't know or cannot answer
